(b) Requirements for new buildings. After March 1, 1991, there shall not be initiated within the boundary limits of the city the construction of any residential or commercial building of any type which:
(1) Employs a gravity tank type, flushometer valve, or flushometer tank toilet that uses more than an average of 1.6 gallons of water per flush;
(2) Employs a shower head that allows a flow of more than an average of 2.5 gallons of water per minute at 60 pounds per square inch of pressure;
(3) Employs a urinal that uses more than an average of 1.0 gallon of water per flush;
(4) Employs a lavatory faucet or lavatory replacement aerator that allows a flow of more than 2.0 gallons of water per minute; or
(5) Employs a kitchen faucet or kitchen replacement aerator that allows a flow of more than 2.5 gallons of water per minute.
(c) Repairs and renovations. The requirements of subsection (b) of this section shall also apply to any residential and commercial construction initiated after March 1, 1991, which involves the repair or renovation of or addition to any existing building when such repair or renovation of or addition to such existing building includes the replacement of toilets or showers or both; however, this section shall not apply to any construction of a residential or commercial building or repair or renovation of any such building the contract for which was entered into prior to March 1, 1991.
(d) Conditions for exemptions and variances. Exemption and/or variance to the requirements of subsections (b) and (c) of this section may be granted by the building inspector of the city in accordance with the procedure hereinafter set out as to new construction and repair or renovation of existing buildings based upon the following conditions:
(1) When the repair or renovation of the existing building does not include the replacement of the plumbing or sewage system servicing toilets, faucets, or shower heads within such existing building;
(2) When such plumbing or sewage system within such existing building, because of its capacity, design, or installation, would not function properly if the toilets, faucets, or shower heads required by this section were installed;
(3) When such system is a well or gravity flow from a spring and is owned privately by an individual for use in such individual's personal residence; or
(4) When the units to be installed are:
a. Specifically designed for use by the handicapped;
b. Specifically designed to withstand unusual abuse or installation in a penal institution; or
c. Toilets for juveniles.
(e) Procedure for granting exemption or variance. Any person entity desiring to obtain an exception and/or variance from the requirements set forth in subsections (b) and (c) of this section shall present the request to the building inspector for a decision of whether this building (commercial or residential) and the construction or renovation or repair is entitled to the exception and/or variance. The building inspector shall require the application for exception to be submitted in writing and on such forms as such inspector so designates with any attachments that such inspector so requires. The building inspector will have ten days from the date of receipt of the application for the exception in which to render a decision. Once rendered, the decision shall be submitted immediately to the applicant in writing from the building inspector. The applicant, if in disagreement with the decision of the building inspector, may appeal the decision to the mayor and council by filing a request for a de novo proceeding before the mayor and council within 30 days of receipt of the decision by the building inspector. The mayor and council will conduct their hearing within 30 days of receipt of the notice of appeal and will render their decision in writing to the applicant within ten days of the conclusion of the hearing. At the hearing, the applicant will be entitled to introduce evidence by testimony or documents, subpoena a witness, and cross examine any witness appearing on behalf of the building inspector, and may be represented by counsel of his choice, and the proceeding will be recorded in accordance with the administrative policies of the city. During the appeal process and until a final order is entered by the mayor and council, the request for appeal will operate as a supersedeas to the building inspector's decision. The mayor and council may affirm, deny, revise, amend, remand for additional proceeding and alter the decision of building inspector.
